summary.headline: Apar Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 21.3% YoY to INR6,931 crore and EBITDA 57.8% to INR787 crore, with a record INR12,025 crore order book.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was INR6,931 crore (+21.3% YoY, +5.2% QoQ) and EBITDA after forex was INR787 crore (+57.8% YoY, margin 11.4%, +270 bps), with PAT up 77.8% to INR447 crore. Roughly INR800 crore of conductor and cable sales on DDP terms were in transit at quarter end, which depressed US revenue (down 29.7% YoY) and conductor/cable dispatches. Conductor volumes fell 9.2% YoY on delayed TBCB clearances and metal-driven customer deferrals, while the oil division's margins were boosted by contract buying and volumes fell about 20%. Management expects Q3 and Q4 conductor volumes to beat H1 and the in-transit revenue to be recognised in Q3.

financial_highlights.change: Revenue +21.1% YoY; EBITDA +11.3% YoY; volume -9.2% YoY

financial_highlights.value: INR1,819 crore; EBITDA INR299 crore; volume 128,590 KL
financial_highlights.change: Revenue +35.6% YoY; EBITDA +185% YoY; volume ~-20% YoY
Credit rating upgraded one notch from AA- to AA

segments.name: Conductors
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR3,753 crore (+21.1% YoY), driven mainly by metal price increases; volume -9.2% YoY. EBITDA per tonne INR48,241 (vs INR39,363 a year ago); premium mix 39.4% (vs 45.3%).

segments.name: Oil (lubricants/base oil)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR1,819 crore (+35.6% YoY); EBITDA INR299 crore. Volumes fell about 20% as management limited sales to contracted, higher-quality customers; export share 37%.

segments.name: Cables
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR1,875 crore (+22.1% YoY) with copper ~30% of mix; US sales down ~50% YoY on in-transit DDP shipments. Cable order book about INR3,000 crore (vs INR1,653 crore), with ~INR1,000 crore from Google and Amazon data centres.

guidance_outlook: Conductor volumes expected to decline less in Q3 and to be stronger in H2 than H1, per Ramesh Iyer.
About INR800 crore of in-transit conductor and cable sales (DDP, mainly US) expected to be recognised in Q3.
Cable revenue growth guided at 25% YoY in value, with management confident of meeting it; cable EBITDA margin target 11-12%.
Management does not give quarterly or annual EBITDA-per-tonne guidance; it cites a 35,000-36,000 per tonne range as the tailwind framework for conductors.
Domestic capex of about INR1,500 crore over 12-15 months, of which about INR500 crore is spent; thereafter annual capex of INR300-400 crore. Overseas expansion not yet included.
Industry conductor growth around 10% in volume terms, or 15-20% in rupee terms at constant metal prices; oil and lubricants guided at 5-7%.
capex_capacity: Domestic capex of about INR1,500 crore over 12-15 months, with about INR500 crore spent so far; annual run-rate thereafter INR300-400 crore.
Overseas expansion under evaluation at an advanced stage; board passed an enabling resolution for up to about USD100 million investment in wholly owned Singapore subsidiary PSPL, with no details yet.
Cable utilisation above 90%, with some copper lines at 100-105% for data centre orders; conductor utilisation about 80%; oil not capacity-constrained.
Silvassa heavy rains cut half of the CTC complex capacity by roughly 90 days of equivalent output in Q2.
Cable voltage upgrade to 132 kV and 220 kV is planned; no business expected in FY27, with FY28 the earliest.
demand_pricing: Conductor order book INR12,025 crore at 30 September, an all-time high; Q2 inflows INR4,725 crore (+82% YoY), including about INR3,000 crore from UK and US utilities.
Q2 orders include a first Z-shaped conductor order from a Scandinavian utility, a KPCL OPGW order of about INR960 crore (48-fibre), and a 144-fibre OPGW order in Central America.

Commodity inflation: copper up about 50% and aluminium up about 35% in the quarter; aluminium MGP at a four-year high; steel prices also up sharply. Freight to Europe and LatAm rose 2-3x, now showing signs of easing.
Management attributes volume declines to TBCB awardees delaying manufacturing clearances, with a 36-month execution limit and heavy penalties on delay.
Chinese competition remains severe because of the SHFE-LME arbitrage; Apar is focusing on utility rate contracts in the US and Europe.
Oil: base oil prices roughly doubled; the company is selling fewer spot and price-sensitive customer volumes, and management says Q2 margins are not normal.

qa_highlights.question: How should the aluminium/conductor EBITDA per tonne be thought of for FY27, given H1 at INR48,000-50,000 against 40,000 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not give quarterly or annual guidance; it cites a 35,000-36,000+ per tonne framework with tailwinds from premium mix, but margins vary by product, customer and geography.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade payable days fall from about 109 to about 81, and what are acceptances?
qa_highlights.answer: QIP money was deployed into working capital, with more cash purchases of raw materials; acceptances were about INR3,500 crore at 26 September.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27 and FY28, and what is the Singapore investment about?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic capex is about INR1,500 crore over 12-15 months with INR500 crore spent; overseas expansion is still being closed. The PSPL resolution is an enabling one for investment in the Singapore subsidiary, with details to come later.

qa_highlights.question: Is cable margin moving to 11-12%, and what is the data centre margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 11-12% and delivered 11% in Q2; US data-centre cables carry higher margins than Indian ones because of higher specifications, while Indian data-centre competition is intense.

qa_highlights.question: Will conductor volumes recover, and has the TBCB delay eased?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the decline to be arrested in Q3 and H2 volumes to be stronger than H1, because of year-end project completion deadlines and penalties.

qa_highlights.question: Is oil Q2 margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says some gain came from buying on contract versus spot; these are not normal margins, and the company will keep limiting volume to quality business.

risks_watch: Metal price volatility (copper, aluminium, steel) and freight costs compressing conductor and cable margins.
About INR800 crore in-transit DDP sales to the US must convert to revenue in Q3; the company said Q3 will look different.
Conductor volume recovery depends on TBCB clearances and customer deferrals; H1 volume was down about 9%.
Oil volumes down about 20% and margins elevated by spot price swings; sustainability is uncertain if the war ends.
Rising competition in HTLS and CTC, and Chinese export competition.
Working capital intensity: lower payable days and high inventory value at commodity prices.
Overseas expansion and the USD100 million PSPL funding remain undisclosed in detail.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book and structural demand, but cautious on near-term conductor volumes and oil margins. Management declined to give quarterly or annual EBITDA-per-tonne guidance and gave limited detail on the overseas capex and PSPL funding.
key_quotes: All of this product is actually scheduled to be sold in the U.S. market.

So considering this prudence, in terms of how much you would be willing to build to customers and what exposures we would be ready to take, we see that the overall volume is down to 128,590 KL for the quarter.
So, by no means, these are normal margins, which are there.
So the whole focus that we have today is to preserve the quality part of the business.
